Este informe detalla la normalización y el control de calidad de un ensayo NanoString Immune-Oncology 360. Se utilizó la herramienta de BioConductor https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/NanoStringNCTools.html para realizar la normalización (nSolver con controles positivos) y el control de calidad.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo    = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  error   = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",   # centrar todas las figuras en el HTML
  fig.width  = 10,        # anchura por defecto para las figuras
  fig.height = 6          # altura por defecto para las figuras
)
```

```{r setup_dirs, include=FALSE}
# =========================================
# ESTRUCTURA DE LA CARPETA DE RESULTADOS
# =========================================
# results/
#   ├── 01_QC/                 → flags de QC + correlaciones de controles pre-normalización
#   ├── 02_raw_counts/         → distribuciones, recuentos crudos, ceros, KDE, outliers
#   ├── 03_normalization/      → normalización POS + correlaciones post-normalización
#   ├── 04_batch_effect/       → metadatos y análisis del efecto batch (limma)

# Establecer manualmente la raíz del proyecto
here::i_am("data/Rawdata/NS_IO_360_2runs.csv")
library(here)

results_dir  <- here("results")
qc_dir       <- file.path(results_dir, "01_QC")
raw_dir      <- file.path(results_dir, "02_raw_counts")
norm_dir     <- file.path(results_dir, "03_normalization")
batch_dir    <- file.path(results_dir, "04_batch_effect")
explor_dir   <- file.path(results_dir, "05_exploratory")

for (d in c(results_dir, qc_dir, raw_dir, norm_dir, batch_dir, explor_dir)) {
  dir.create(d, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
}

# Función auxiliar: guarda el gráfico activo (base o ggplot) y lo vuelve a mostrar
save_and_show <- function(plot_obj = NULL, path, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300) {
  if (!is.null(plot_obj)) {
    
    # caso pheatmap: devuelve una lista con un elemento $gtable
    if (is.list(plot_obj) && "gtable" %in% names(plot_obj)) {
      # Guardar en fichero
      png(path, width = width * dpi, height = height * dpi, res = dpi)
      grid::grid.draw(plot_obj$gtable)
      dev.off()
      # Renderizar en el HTML
      grid::grid.newpage()
      grid::grid.draw(plot_obj$gtable)
      
    } else {
      # ggplot o similar
      ggplot2::ggsave(path, plot = plot_obj, width = width, height = height,
                      units = "in", dpi = dpi, bg = "white")
      print(plot_obj)
    }
    
  } else {
    # gráficos base de R
    png(path, width = width * dpi, height = height * dpi, res = dpi)
    replayPlot(recordPlot())
    dev.off()
  }
}
```

```{r helper_tablas_correlacion, include=FALSE}
# =========================================
# FUNCIONES AUXILIARES PARA LAS FIGURAS DE TABLAS DE CORRELACIÓN
# =========================================
library(gridExtra)
library(grid)
library(gtable)
library(dplyr)

# Construye un grob de tabla (Gen / r / valor p) con título de subgrupo
.make_corr_grob <- function(df, subtitulo, color_cabecera) {
  tbl <- df %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(abs(Correlation))) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Gen            = Gene,
      `r (Spearman)` = round(Correlation, 3),
      `Valor p`      = formatC(P_value, format = "e", digits = 2)
    )

  th <- gridExtra::ttheme_minimal(
    base_size = 9,
    core    = list(fg_params = list(hjust = 0.5, x = 0.5),
                   bg_params = list(fill = c("grey97", "white"), col = "grey90")),
    colhead = list(fg_params = list(col = "white", fontface = "bold"),
                   bg_params = list(fill = color_cabecera, col = NA))
  )

  g <- gridExtra::tableGrob(tbl, rows = NULL, theme = th)

  # Añadir el subtítulo encima de la tabla
  titulo  <- grid::textGrob(subtitulo, gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 11, fontface = "bold"))
  g <- gtable::gtable_add_rows(g, heights = grid::grobHeight(titulo) + grid::unit(4, "mm"), pos = 0)
  g <- gtable::gtable_add_grob(g, titulo, t = 1, l = 1, r = ncol(g))
  g
}

# Genera la figura con las 3 tablas (positivos / housekeeping / negativos)
generar_figura_correlaciones <- function(pos_tbl, hk_tbl, neg_tbl,
                                         titulo_principal, ruta_png,
                                         width = 15, height = 9, dpi = 300) {
  g_pos <- .make_corr_grob(pos_tbl, "Controles Positivos",  "lightskyblue")
  g_hk  <- .make_corr_grob(hk_tbl,  "Genes Housekeeping",    "khaki")
  g_neg <- .make_corr_grob(neg_tbl, "Controles Negativos",  "lightsteelblue")

  figura <- gridExtra::arrangeGrob(
    grobs = list(g_pos, g_hk, g_neg),
    nrow  = 1,
    top   = grid::textGrob(titulo_principal,
                           gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "bold"))
  )

  ggplot2::ggsave(ruta_png, figura, width = width, height = height,
                  dpi = dpi, bg = "white")
  grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(figura)   # también la muestra en el HTML
  invisible(ruta_png)
}
```

## 1. Rutas y Ficheros

```{r rutas_y_archivos}
datadir               <- here("data", "Rawdata")
rlf_file              <- file.path(datadir, "NS_IO_360_v1.0.rlf")
sample_annotation_file <- file.path(datadir, "NS_IO_360_2runs.csv")

read_sample_annotation <- function(file_path) {
  sample_data   <- read.csv(file_path, check.names = FALSE,
                             stringsAsFactors = FALSE, header = FALSE)
  sample_data_t <- as.data.frame(t(sample_data), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  colnames(sample_data_t) <- sample_data_t[1, ]
  sample_data_t <- sample_data_t[-1, ]

  if (!all(c("File Name", "Sample ID") %in% colnames(sample_data_t))) {
    stop("No se encontraron las columnas 'File Name' y/o 'Sample ID' en el CSV.")
  }
  sample_data_t <- sample_data_t[, c("File Name", "Sample ID", "Run", "SampleType")]
  sample_data_t <- sample_data_t[!is.na(sample_data_t$`File Name`) &
                                   sample_data_t$`File Name` != "", ]
  sample_data_t <- sample_data_t[!is.na(sample_data_t$`Sample ID`) &
                                   sample_data_t$`Sample ID` != "", ]
  sample_data_t
}

sample_data_t <- read_sample_annotation(sample_annotation_file)

rcc_files  <- list.files(datadir, pattern = "\\.RCC$", full.names = TRUE)
rcc_names  <- basename(rcc_files)
missing_files <- setdiff(sample_data_t$`File Name`, rcc_names)
if (length(missing_files) > 0) {
  warning("Faltan ficheros RCC: ", paste(missing_files, collapse = ", "))
} else {
  message("Todos los ficheros RCC están presentes.")
}
```

## 4. Exploración de los Datos Crudos

```{r Gene_counts_distribution, fig.width=14, fig.height=7}
library(tidyverse)

# Convertir los datos a data.frame
data_df   <- as.data.frame(nanoStringData)
# Identificar las columnas de expresión (todas las que empiezan por 'Endogenous_')
expr_cols <- grep("^Endogenous_", colnames(data_df), value = TRUE)
# Transformar a formato largo
data_long <- pivot_longer(data_df, 
                          cols = all_of(expr_cols),
                          names_to = "Gene", 
                          values_to = "Expression")

# Generar automáticamente la paleta de colores según el número de muestras
n_samples     <- length(unique(data_long$Sample.ID))
color_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("lightskyblue2", "magenta4", "coral1", "olivedrab3"))(n_samples)

# Boxplot crudo
expression_plot <- ggplot(data_long, aes(x = Sample.ID, y = Expression, fill = Sample.ID)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_palette) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Distribución de la Expresión (Recuentos Crudos)",
       x = "Muestras", y = "Expresión") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 8),
        legend.position = "none")

print(expression_plot)
ggsave(file.path(raw_dir, "boxplot_expression_raw.png"),
       expression_plot, width = 14, height = 7, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# Boxplot log2
log2expression_plot <- ggplot(data_long,
                               aes(x = Sample.ID, y = log2(Expression + 1), fill = Sample.ID)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.8, outlier.shape = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_palette) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Distribución de la Expresión (log2)",
       x = "Muestras", y = "log2(Expresión + 1)") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 8),
        legend.position = "none")

print(log2expression_plot)
ggsave(file.path(raw_dir, "boxplot_log2expression_raw.png"),
       log2expression_plot, width = 14, height = 7, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# Barplot de recuentos totales
blues  <- colorRampPalette(c("lightskyblue2", "magenta4"))(12)
corals <- colorRampPalette(c("coral1", "olivedrab3"))(12)
color_palette <- c(blues, corals)

total_counts_df <- data_long %>%
  group_by(Sample.ID) %>%
  summarise(TotalCounts = sum(Expression, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

total_counts_plot <- ggplot(total_counts_df,
                             aes(x = Sample.ID, y = TotalCounts, fill = Sample.ID)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_palette) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Recuentos Totales por Muestra", x = "Muestras", y = "Recuentos Totales") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 8),
        legend.position = "none") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(TotalCounts)), vjust = -0.5, size = 3)

print(total_counts_plot)
ggsave(file.path(raw_dir, "barplot_total_counts.png"),
       total_counts_plot, width = 14, height = 7, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# Resumen de recuentos a cero
count_matrix       <- exprs(nanoStringData)
zero_counts        <- as.data.frame(count_matrix == 0)
names(zero_counts) <- sampleNames(nanoStringData)
rownames(zero_counts) <- featureNames(nanoStringData)

zero_counts_summary <- colSums(zero_counts)
write.csv(data.frame(Sample = names(zero_counts_summary),
                     Genes_with_zero_counts = zero_counts_summary),
          file.path(raw_dir, "zero_counts_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

genes_with_zero <- zero_counts[rowSums(zero_counts) > 0, ]
genes_with_zero <- genes_with_zero[order(rowSums(genes_with_zero), decreasing = TRUE), ]
write.csv(genes_with_zero, file.path(raw_dir, "genes_with_zero_counts.csv"))
```

## 5. Distribución KDE por Muestra

```{r KDE_Plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
exprs_df <- as.data.frame(exprs(nanoStringData))
exprs_long <- gather(exprs_df, key = "Sample", value = "Expression", 1:ncol(exprs_df))
exprs_long$Gene <- rep(rownames(exprs(nanoStringData)), each = ncol(exprs(nanoStringData)))

# Definir las muestras destacadas
highlight_samples <- c(
  "20260310_IO360RunB_HON2545_05.RCC",
  "20260310_IO360RunB_HON2534_09.RCC",
  "20260310_IO360RunB_StandardRUNB_12.RCC",
  "20260304_IO360RunA_StandardRUNA_12.RCC"
)

# Crear una columna de grupo para la asignación de color
exprs_long$Group <- ifelse(exprs_long$Sample %in% highlight_samples,
                           exprs_long$Sample,
                           "Other")

# Definir la paleta de colores
color_values <- c(
  "Other"                                      = "grey70",
  "20260310_IO360RunB_HON2545_05.RCC"          = "maroon",      # muestra HK límite (borderline)
  "20260310_IO360RunB_HON2534_09.RCC"          = "orange",      # muestra outlier detectada por KS
  "20260310_IO360RunB_StandardRUNB_12.RCC"     = "steelblue1",
  "20260304_IO360RunA_StandardRUNA_12.RCC"     = "dodgerblue"
)

density_plot <- ggplot(exprs_long, aes(x = Expression, color = Group, group = Sample)) +
  geom_density(data = subset(exprs_long, Group == "Other"), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_density(data = subset(exprs_long, Group != "Other"), alpha = 0.9, linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = color_values,
    breaks = highlight_samples,   # solo las muestras destacadas aparecen en la leyenda
    name   = "Muestras Destacadas"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-500, 3000)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Distribución de la Expresión por Muestra (KDE – Datos Crudos)",
       x = "Expresión (recuentos)", y = "Densidad")

print(density_plot)
ggsave(file.path(raw_dir, "KDE_expression_raw.png"),
       density_plot, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# --- 5.1 Muestras Outlier Usando el Método KS ---
# Muestras no biológicas a excluir del test KS
standards <- c(
  "20260310_IO360RunB_StandardRUNB_12.RCC",
  "20260304_IO360RunA_StandardRUNA_12.RCC"
)

# Subconjunto solo con muestras biológicas
exprs_long_bio <- exprs_long %>% filter(!Sample %in% standards)

# Calcular las métricas de distribución
dist_metrics <- exprs_long_bio %>%
  group_by(Sample) %>%
  summarise(
    Median      = median(Expression),
    MAD          = mad(Expression),
    KS_Distance = ks.test(Expression, ecdf(exprs_long_bio$Expression))$statistic
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(KS_Distance))

# Muestras outlier del 8% superior
threshold            <- quantile(dist_metrics$KS_Distance, 0.92)
outlier_samples <- dist_metrics %>% filter(KS_Distance > threshold) %>% pull(Sample)
outlier_colors  <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(n = max(3, length(outlier_samples)), "Set2")

p_outliers <- ggplot(exprs_long_bio, aes(x = Expression)) +
  geom_density(data = subset(exprs_long_bio, !(Sample %in% outlier_samples)),
               color = "gray80", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_density(data = subset(exprs_long_bio, Sample %in% outlier_samples),
               aes(color = Sample, fill = Sample), alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(title = paste("Muestras Outlier:", length(outlier_samples)),
       subtitle = "Basado en la distancia KS (estándares excluidos)",
       x = "Expresión (recuentos)", y = "Densidad") +
  scale_color_manual(values = outlier_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = outlier_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-500, 3000)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(p_outliers)
ggsave(file.path(raw_dir, "KDE_outlier_samples.png"),
       p_outliers, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```
## 6. Correlación Pre-Normalización
```{r Correlation_pre_norm, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
n_samples <- ncol(exprs(nanoStringData))
color_palette <- colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Set2"))(n_samples)

analyze_gene_class <- function(nanoStringData, gene_class, title_name) {
  # Extraer datos
  total_counts <- colSums(exprs(nanoStringData))
  
  # Determinar el prefijo según la clase de gen
  prefix <- switch(gene_class,
                  "Positive" = "POS_",
                  "Negative" = "NEG_",
                  "Housekeeping" = "Housekeeping_",
                  "")
  
  class_expr <- exprs(nanoStringData)[fData(nanoStringData)$CodeClass == gene_class, ]
  
# Simplificar los nombres de muestra — también cubre StandardRUN
modified_sample_names <- sapply(colnames(class_expr), function(x) {
  parts <- unlist(strsplit(x, "_"))
  hon_idx <- grep("HON", parts)
  if(length(hon_idx) > 0) return(parts[hon_idx])
  # StandardRUN
  std_idx <- grep("StandardRUN", parts)
  if(length(std_idx) > 0) {
    run_id <- sub("StandardRUN", "Std_Run", parts[std_idx])
    return(run_id)
  }
  x
})
  
  colnames(class_expr) <- modified_sample_names
  
  # Datos del boxplot (se devuelven para combinarlos después)
  df_box <- as.data.frame(t(class_expr))
  df_box$Sample <- rownames(df_box)
  df_long_box <- gather(df_box, key = "Gene", value = "Count", -Sample)
  df_long_box$Class <- title_name
  
  # Limpiar los nombres de los genes
  modified_gene_names <- sapply(rownames(class_expr), function(x) {
    x_no_prefix <- sub(paste0("^", prefix), "", x)
    sub("_NM.*$", "", x_no_prefix)
  })
  
  rownames(class_expr) <- modified_gene_names
  
  # Gráfico de correlación con valores p
  df_cor <- data.frame(
    Sample = colnames(class_expr),
    Total_Counts = total_counts,
    t(class_expr)
  ) %>% 
    pivot_longer(
      cols = -c(Sample, Total_Counts),
      names_to = "Gene",
      values_to = "Expression"
    ) %>% 
    group_by(Gene) %>% 
    mutate(
      Correlation = cor(Total_Counts, Expression, method = "spearman"),
      P_value = cor.test(Total_Counts, Expression, method = "spearman")$p.value,
      Label_r = paste0(Gene, " (r = ", round(Correlation, 2), 
                          ", p = ", formatC(P_value, format = "e", digits = 2), ")")
    ) %>% 
    ungroup()
  
  p_cor <- ggplot(df_cor, aes(x = Total_Counts, y = Expression, color = Label_r)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma, trans = "log10") +
    scale_y_continuous(trans = "log10") +
    labs(
      title = paste(title_name, "— Expresión vs. Recuentos Totales"),
      subtitle = "Relación con los recuentos totales por muestra",
      x = "Recuentos Totales (log10)",
      y = paste(title_name, "— Expresión (log10)"),
      color = title_name
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
  
  # Tabla de correlación con valores p
  cor_table <- df_cor %>% 
    distinct(Gene, Correlation, P_value) %>% 
    arrange(desc(Correlation))
  
  list(
    boxplot_data = df_long_box,
    correlation_plot = p_cor,
    correlation_table = cor_table
  )
}
```

```{r Normalization, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =========================================
# 7.1 Normalización nSolver
# =========================================
nanoStringData_norm <- normalize(
  nanoStringData,
  type    = "nSolver",
  fromELT = "exprs",
  toELT   = "exprs_norm"
)

# =========================================
# 7.2 Función de Análisis por Clase de Gen (Post-Normalización)
# =========================================
analyze_gene_class <- function(nanoStringData_obj, gene_class, title_name, color_palette,
                               elt = "exprs") {
  expr_data      <- assayDataElement(nanoStringData_obj, elt)
  total_counts <- colSums(expr_data)
  class_expr     <- expr_data[fData(nanoStringData_obj)$CodeClass == gene_class, ]

  prefix <- switch(gene_class,
                   "Positive"     = "POS_",
                   "Negative"     = "NEG_",
                   "Housekeeping" = "Housekeeping_",
                   "")

  # Simplificar los nombres de muestra (HON + StandardRUN)
  modified_sample_names <- sapply(colnames(class_expr), function(x) {
    parts <- unlist(strsplit(x, "_"))
    hon_idx <- grep("HON", parts)
    if (length(hon_idx) > 0) return(parts[hon_idx])
    std_idx <- grep("StandardRUN", parts)
    if (length(std_idx) > 0) return(sub("StandardRUN", "Std_Run", parts[std_idx]))
    x
  })
  colnames(class_expr) <- modified_sample_names

  # Datos del boxplot (para combinarlos después)
  df_box <- as.data.frame(t(class_expr))
  df_box$Sample <- rownames(df_box)
  df_long_box <- gather(df_box, key = "Gene", value = "Count", -Sample)
  df_long_box$Class <- title_name

  # Limpiar los nombres de los genes
  modified_gene_names <- sapply(rownames(class_expr), function(x) {
    x_no_prefix <- sub(paste0("^", prefix), "", x)
    sub("_NM.*$", "", x_no_prefix)
  })
  rownames(class_expr) <- modified_gene_names

  # Correlación con valores p
  df_cor <- data.frame(
    Sample        = colnames(class_expr),
    Total_Counts = total_counts,
    t(class_expr)
  ) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols      = -c(Sample, Total_Counts),
      names_to  = "Gene",
      values_to = "Expression"
    ) %>%
    group_by(Gene) %>%
    mutate(
      Correlation = cor(Total_Counts, Expression, method = "spearman"),
      P_value = suppressWarnings(cor.test(Total_Counts, Expression, method = "spearman"))$p.value,
      Label_r = paste0(Gene, " (r = ", round(Correlation, 2),
                          ", p = ", formatC(P_value, format = "e", digits = 2), ")")
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

  gene_order <- df_cor %>% distinct(Gene, Correlation, Label_r) %>% arrange(desc(abs(Correlation)))
  df_cor$Label_r <- factor(df_cor$Label_r, levels = gene_order$Label_r)

  p_cor <- ggplot(df_cor, aes(x = Total_Counts, y = Expression, color = Label_r)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
    labs(
      title    = paste(title_name, "— Expresión vs. Recuentos Totales"),
      subtitle = "Post-Normalización POS",
      x = "Recuentos Totales (log10)",
      y = paste(title_name, "— Expresión (log10)"),
      color = title_name
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

  cor_table <- df_cor %>%
    distinct(Gene, Correlation, P_value) %>%
    arrange(desc(abs(Correlation)))

  list(boxplot_data = df_long_box, correlation_plot = p_cor, correlation_table = cor_table)
}

# =========================================
# 7.3 Análisis Post-Normalización POS
# =========================================
n_samples <- ncol(exprs(nanoStringData_norm))
color_palette <- colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Set2"))(n_samples)

positive_results     <- analyze_gene_class(nanoStringData_norm, "Positive",
                                           "Controles Positivos", color_palette,
                                           elt = "exprs_norm")
housekeeping_results <- analyze_gene_class(nanoStringData_norm, "Housekeeping",
                                           "Genes Housekeeping", color_palette,
                                           elt = "exprs_norm")
negative_results     <- analyze_gene_class(nanoStringData_norm, "Negative",
                                           "Controles Negativos", color_palette,
                                           elt = "exprs_norm")

# --- Boxplot Combinado Post-Normalización ---
combined_box_data <- bind_rows(
  positive_results$boxplot_data,
  housekeeping_results$boxplot_data,
  negative_results$boxplot_data
)

combined_box_data$Class <- factor(combined_box_data$Class,
                                  levels = c("Controles Positivos", "Genes Housekeeping", "Controles Negativos"))

p_box_combined <- ggplot(combined_box_data, aes(x = Sample, y = Count, fill = Sample)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.8, alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  facet_wrap(~ Class, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribución de Controles y Housekeeping (Post-Normalización POS)",
    subtitle = "Distribución entre muestras por clase de gen",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Recuentos (log10)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 6),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_palette) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.10, NA))

# Mostrar
p_box_combined
positive_results$correlation_plot
print(positive_results$correlation_table)
housekeeping_results$correlation_plot
print(housekeeping_results$correlation_table)
negative_results$correlation_plot
print(negative_results$correlation_table)

# Guardar gráficos individuales
save_and_show(p_box_combined, file.path(norm_dir, "boxplot_combined_postnorm.png"))
save_and_show(positive_results$correlation_plot, file.path(norm_dir, "correlation_positive_controls.png"))
save_and_show(negative_results$correlation_plot, file.path(norm_dir, "correlation_negative_controls.png"))
save_and_show(housekeeping_results$correlation_plot, file.path(norm_dir, "correlation_housekeeping_genes.png"))

write.csv(positive_results$correlation_table,     file.path(norm_dir, "correlation_table_positive_controls.csv"),  row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(negative_results$correlation_table,     file.path(norm_dir, "correlation_table_negative_controls.csv"),  row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(housekeeping_results$correlation_table, file.path(norm_dir, "correlation_table_housekeeping_genes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# =========================================
# 7.4 Guardar la Matriz Normalizada Final
# =========================================
final_norm_data <- assayDataElement(nanoStringData_norm, "exprs_norm")
write.csv(final_norm_data, file.path(norm_dir, "final_normalized_matrix.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

boxplot(log2(final_norm_data + 1),  main = "Normalizado nSolver",   las = 2, col = "khaki")

# --- PDF POST-NORMALIZACIÓN ---
pdf(file.path(norm_dir, "All_plots_post_normalization.pdf"), width = 14, height = 8)
  print(p_box_combined)
  print(positive_results$correlation_plot)
  print(housekeeping_results$correlation_plot)
  print(negative_results$correlation_plot)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(8, 4, 4, 2))
```

## 8. Efecto Batch

```{r Batch_Effect}
# Cargar los paquetes necesarios
pacman::p_load(
  ggplot2, 
  ggrepel,
  pheatmap,
  RColorBrewer,
  limma,
  lme4,
  variancePartition,
  dplyr,
  reshape2,
  Biobase,
  gridExtra,
  patchwork
)

# Extraer la matriz de expresión (ExpressionSet o data frame/matriz)
expr_matrix <- if (is(final_norm_data, "ExpressionSet")) {
  Biobase::exprs(final_norm_data)
} else {
  as.matrix(final_norm_data)
}

# Limpiar los nombres de muestra
clean_sample_names <- colnames(expr_matrix)

# Crear los metadatos a partir de la anotación de muestras (sample_data_t)
# Emparejar los nombres de fichero RCC con las columnas Run y SampleType
metadata <- data.frame(
  SampleID   = clean_sample_names,
  row.names  = clean_sample_names
)

# Cruzar con sample_data_t para obtener Run y SampleType
annot_match <- match(clean_sample_names, sample_data_t$`File Name`)
metadata$Batch      <- factor(sample_data_t$Run[annot_match])
metadata$SampleType <- factor(sample_data_t$SampleType[annot_match])

# Avisar si alguna muestra no se ha podido emparejar
if (any(is.na(annot_match))) {
  warning("No se encontró anotación para: ",
          paste(clean_sample_names[is.na(annot_match)], collapse = ", "))
}

write.csv(metadata, file.path(batch_dir, "metadata.csv"))

# =========================================
# 8.1 Análisis Estadístico con limma (Efecto Batch)
# =========================================
if (nlevels(metadata$Batch) > 1) {
  design <- model.matrix(~ Batch, data = metadata)
  fit <- lmFit(expr_matrix, design) |> eBayes()
  batch_results <- topTable(fit, coef = 2, number = Inf, sort.by = "none")

# Histograma para analizar la distribución de los valores p asociados al efecto batch para todos los genes
pval_plot <- ggplot(batch_results, aes(x = P.Value)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 0.8) +
    labs(title = "Distribución de Valores p (Efecto Batch)") +
    theme_minimal()

  save_and_show(pval_plot, file.path(batch_dir, "pvalue_distribution.png"), width = 8, height = 6)
  write.csv(batch_results, file.path(batch_dir, "limma_batch_results.csv"), row.names = TRUE)
} else {
  message("Solo hay un nivel de Batch en los metadatos. ",
          "Se omite el análisis del efecto batch con limma. ",
          "Actualiza la columna 'Batch' de los metadatos con los runs reales.")
}
```

```{r Exploratory_PCA, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# =========================================
# 9.1 PCA

pca_result <- prcomp(t(expr_matrix), scale. = TRUE)
pca_vars <- round(100 * pca_result$sdev^2 / sum(pca_result$sdev^2), 1)

pca_data <- data.frame(
  PC1 = pca_result$x[,1],
  PC2 = pca_result$x[,2],
  Sample = clean_sample_names,
  Batch = metadata$Batch,
  SampleType = metadata$SampleType
)

pca_plot <- ggplot(pca_data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, label = Sample,
                                  color = Batch, shape = SampleType)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA de Todas las Muestras",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", pca_vars[1], "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", pca_vars[2], "%)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

save_and_show(pca_plot, file.path(explor_dir, "pca_plot.png"), width = 10, height = 8)
```

```{r Exploratory_Outliers, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# =========================================
# 9.5 Detección de Outliers (Correlación de Spearman)
# =========================================
cor_matrix_sp <- cor(expr_matrix, method = "spearman")
mean_cor <- rowMeans(cor_matrix_sp)
cor_threshold <- 0.5
outlier_flag <- ifelse(mean_cor < cor_threshold, "Outlier", "Normal")

annotation_df <- data.frame(
  Mean_Correlation = mean_cor,
  Status = outlier_flag
)
rownames(annotation_df) <- clean_sample_names

spearman_path <- file.path(explor_dir, "heatmap_spearman_outliers.png")

pheatmap(cor_matrix_sp,
         color = colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(9, "YlOrRd"))(100),
         annotation_row = annotation_df,
         annotation_col = annotation_df,
         show_rownames = TRUE,
         show_colnames = FALSE,
         fontsize = 8,
         main = paste("Correlación de Spearman | Outliers (cor <", cor_threshold, ")"),
         filename = spearman_path)

knitr::include_graphics(spearman_path)
```
